slug: 2024-04-23 The Gambia Social Registry - A Success Story in Systems Building

facts.fact: The World Bank blog says the Gambia Social Registry (GamSR), covering 203,022 households in 40 of 43 districts, underpinned the Nafa Quick COVID-19 response (78,422 households) and the Nafa cash-transfer programme (16,966 households), and is also used by the National Disaster Management Agency, the ROOTS project and the World Food Programme; no event date is given, so the publication date is used.

note: No statement of a link to the national ID, a payment provider or another sector's system; only shared use of the registry.
The story names no social protection system or link.

slug: 2025-07-15 Global Insights on Social Registries - Coverage and Beyond (World Bank)
note: Global reference report held as an excerpt page; it names The Gambia's social registry as a comparator and states nothing on exchange, sharing or links.

facts.fact: The World Bank's November 2025 status report on the RISE project says complementary systems strengthening, including social registry enhancements and interoperability efforts, progressed, without naming the systems linked.

note: Interoperability efforts are stated without naming the systems linked; date taken from the report's archive date of 2025-11-29.

facts.fact: The World Bank framework says Gambian social protection agencies operate in silos with little information shared across them, and that the Department of Social Welfare and Community Development hold no functional information systems; the date is the document's published year, as it gives none for the finding (its missions ran November 2017 to May 2018).
facts.system: Social protection programmes of The Gambia

facts.fact: The framework says the Maternal and Child Nutrition and Health Results Project (NaNA, World Bank-supported) handles beneficiary lists, payment calculation and data exchange manually in Excel files, with data sharing by e-mail and no database; the date is the document's published year.

The framework says MCNHRP payments are made manually, although a pilot test was running to pay beneficiaries by mobile money through a private service provider, Qcell; the date is the document's published year.
